items.title: Integrability and centering of a completed Ito process at bounded stopping times

source.edition: Samplinglib main, commit 2fdbd600d7fe4731458dc7cde2184fd4fdaf7e02, with pinned Mathlib 4.33.0
source.attribution: Samplinglib packages the standard bounded stopped-Ito integrability and zero-mean consequences of its constructed completed process.

items.statement: For a progressive square-integrable real integrand on a positive finite horizon, evaluating its completed continuous Ito process at a nonnegative stopping time bounded pointwise by the horizon gives an integrable random variable of expectation zero.
assumptions: A progressive L2 integrand on a positive NNReal horizon T.
A Brownian motion relative to the filtration and ambient measure, and the usual filtration conditions.
An NNReal-valued stopping time tau with tau(omega)≤T for every omega.
An ambient finite-measure instance, already entailed by the Brownian probability contract and used by the completed-process API.

obligations.label: Transfer terminal L2 integrability to bounded random-time evaluation
Derive zero expectation from the stopped-integrand martingale and random-stopping identity

bindings.boundary: No unbounded stopping, local-L2 localization, vector stochastic integral, general optional sampling, quadratic variation, or Ito formula is asserted.

assumption_deltas.source: The completed bounded random-stopping identity identifies the stopped terminal integral with process evaluation at tau.
assumption_deltas.lean: The Lean theorem combines that identity with terminalRepresentative_integrable, retaining the positive horizon, pointwise tau≤T, Chewi stopping-time, Brownian, and usual-condition interfaces; the explicit finite-measure instance is redundant with the probability normalization carried by hB.
assumption_deltas.reason: Every condition used by the completed construction and a.e. identification remains explicit; the conclusion adds only the L1 consequence.

bindings.boundary: The conclusion concerns only the constructed real completed Ito process at a pointwise bounded NNReal stopping time. It is not a general optional-sampling or Ito-formula theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: A square-integrable Ito integral stopped before its finite horizon is a centered martingale value.
assumption_deltas.lean: The Lean theorem applies Martingale.setIntegral_eq to the completed process of the stopped integrand at deterministic times 0 and T, then uses the existing completed random-stopping identity.
assumption_deltas.reason: The construction exposes the progressive-L2, Brownian, usual-condition, stopping-time, and horizon-bound hypotheses needed for the standard argument.
